questions.stem: This figure shows a balloon-tipped catheter advanced through the right heart into a pulmonary artery branch, with characteristic RA, RV, PA, and wedge pressure waveforms. When the balloon is wedged, the measured pressure most closely estimates which value?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Left atrial (left ventricular end-diastolic) pressure, reflecting left-heart preload

explanation.summary: With the balloon wedged, forward pulmonary artery flow is occluded and the catheter tip senses pressure transmitted back through the pulmonary capillary bed from the left atrium. The pulmonary artery wedge (occlusion) pressure therefore approximates left atrial pressure and left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, a measure of left-heart preload.
explanation.whyCorrect: With the balloon wedged, forward pulmonary artery flow is occluded and the catheter tip senses pressure transmitted back through the pulmonary capillary bed from the left atrium. The pulmonary artery wedge (occlusion) pressure therefore approximates left atrial pressure and left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, a measure of left-heart preload.

questions.stem: This chest radiograph shows enlarged central pulmonary vessels, hazy interstitial markings extending toward the lung bases, and an enlarged cardiac silhouette. These findings are most consistent with which condition?

explanation.summary: Enlarged central pulmonary vessels (pulmonary venous congestion), interstitial edema, and cardiomegaly indicate raised left atrial/pulmonary venous pressure, i.e., cardiogenic pulmonary edema from left-heart failure. Pneumonia is typically focal/consolidative, pneumothorax shows lucency with lung collapse, and fibrosis/emphysema have distinct chronic patterns.
explanation.whyCorrect: Enlarged central pulmonary vessels (pulmonary venous congestion), interstitial edema, and cardiomegaly indicate raised left atrial/pulmonary venous pressure, i.e., cardiogenic pulmonary edema from left-heart failure. Pneumonia is typically focal/consolidative, pneumothorax shows lucency with lung collapse, and fibrosis/emphysema have distinct chronic patterns.

questions.stem: This signaling diagram shows dobutamine acting via beta-1/Gs/adenylyl cyclase to raise cAMP, while a second drug blocks PDE3; both converge on increased intracellular Ca2+ and contractility. By what mechanism does the PDE3-blocking drug (milrinone) increase contractility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It inhibits the Na+/K+-ATPase like a cardiac glycoside

choices.label: B
choices.text: It inhibits phosphodiesterase-3, preventing cAMP breakdown so cAMP levels rise

choices.label: C
choices.text: It opens L-type calcium channels directly

choices.label: D
choices.text: It directly stimulates the beta-1 adrenergic receptor

choices.label: E
choices.text: It increases nitric oxide production in the myocyte

explanation.summary: Milrinone inhibits PDE3, the enzyme that degrades cAMP. With cAMP breakdown blocked, intracellular cAMP accumulates, raising Ca2+ and augmenting contractility, an inotropic effect that does not require the beta-receptor (unlike dobutamine, which works upstream through beta-1/Gs/adenylyl cyclase).
explanation.whyCorrect: Milrinone inhibits PDE3, the enzyme that degrades cAMP. With cAMP breakdown blocked, intracellular cAMP accumulates, raising Ca2+ and augmenting contractility, an inotropic effect that does not require the beta-receptor (unlike dobutamine, which works upstream through beta-1/Gs/adenylyl cyclase).

questions.stem: These paired illustrations show a device positioned in the descending aorta that is expanded during diastole and collapsed during systole. What is this therapeutic device?

explanation.summary: The intra-aortic balloon pump inflates in diastole (augmenting coronary perfusion pressure) and deflates just before systole (reducing afterload), improving myocardial oxygen supply and cardiac output. This counterpulsation is used as mechanical support in cardiogenic shock.
